elaine (sec-eng): Heads-up — found a libssl/glibc compatibility surface during CVE-2026-0XXX triage affecting both alpine:3.18 and ubuntu:22.04 base images. Patch exists upstream for OpenSSL but musl/glibc differences mean some sidecars fail. Need prioritization + signer/RBAC checks for the rebuild pipeline.
ryan (eng-runtime): Do we have a reproducible failing container? I can run integration smoke on runtime nodes.
jia (eng-infra): I spun up a quick pod with alpine:3.18 + our app; `ldd` shows mismatch for libcrypto symbols. failing binary exits 127. Details: `segfault` in our fuzz harness.
owen (eng-sre): Let's not blast all images at once. Proposed plan: patch-build -> internal canary (10% infra) -> traffic-shift -> full promotion. Need audit trail for each step.
tom (sec-eng): CVSS 7.5 (tentative), public exploit PoC exists. Recommend expedite but coordinate with RBAC for signer key so we don't block signed-image promotion.
sasha (product-security): Customers on Dedicated might need advance notice. Also check KMS key rotation window — we don't want signatures to fail during rotation.
anil (eng-platform): Current image signer role is `projects/redwood/keys/image-signer`. Who has that IAM? @jia can you post a quick IAM dump? We should ensure CI runner account retains sign permission during rebuilds.
jia (eng-infra): IAM dump: `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeySigner` assigned to `ci-runner@redwood-infra`. Service account is active. But rotation is scheduled tomorrow 03:00 UTC. We can delay rotation 6 hours if needed.
elaine (sec-eng): Good catch. We also need audit logging to capture: build id, image digest, signer key version, and promotable tag. Add a field in the build metadata: `kms_key_version` and `cosign_sig`.
ryan (eng-runtime): On the runtime side, we'll add a preflight that validates library symlinks and ld paths. Quick snippet to run in CI:
```bash
# preflight check
set -e
docker run --rm --entrypoint sh $IMAGE -c '\
  ldd /usr/local/bin/myapp || true; \\n  readelf -s /usr/local/bin/myapp | grep SSL'
```
owen (eng-sre): Canary tagging convention: `redwood/base:ubuntu-22.04-sslpatch-canary-<buildnum>`. Canary promotion must write to audit log with `deployment_phase=canary`. Ops will monitor 6h.
tom (sec-eng): Prioritization matrix: (1) Hosted API infra images that touch crypto -> P0, (2) Dedicated infra images (customer-facing) -> P1, (3) internal tooling containers -> P2. Anyone disagree?
sasha (product-security): +1. Also put embargoed disclosure hold until coordinated release. We should not call out vendor names in public slack.
elaine (sec-eng): Rebuild job name: `rebuild/base-ssl-compat-1945`. CI job will: pull base, apply distro patch, run unit smoke, run runtime preflight, sign with cosign using GCP KMS, push to staging registry.
anjil (typo-reply): (ignored)
anjil removed
anil (eng-platform): For signing we use `cosign` with KMS: `cosign sign --key gcpkms://projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/infra/cryptoKeys/image-signer/cryptoKeyVersions/1 $IMAGE`. Ensure `--annotations kms_key_version=1` is recorded.
jia (eng-infra): Deploy-bot triggered CI job: `rebuild/base-ssl-compat-1945` — starting build.
deploy-bot: CI job `rebuild/base-ssl-compat-1945` queued (jenkins/infra).
ryan (eng-runtime): If canary fails, plan to revert to previous image digest and block promotion. Add automated rollback script to pipeline.
elaine (sec-eng): Add to checklist: `RBAC confirm` (owner/maintainer can't be revoked during promotion), `KMS rotation freeze window` (T-minus 2h during promotion), `Audit enablement` (log exports to secure bucket), `Canary watch 6h`.
sasha (product-security): I'll draft customer notification template for Dedicated customers and legal for embargo timelines.
jia (eng-infra): Build finished: `sha256:abc123...`. Ran preflight; `ldd` warnings present for one micro sidecar. Marking for manual verification.
own (eng-sre): Manual verification: sidecar container crashes on startup in stage when linked against `/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1`. Workaround: rebuild that sidecar with musl-compatible compile flags or use glibc-compat layer. Which do we prefer?\rtom (sec-eng): For the short term, prefer rebuilding sidecar with musl flags (small change). For longer term, maintain a glibc-compat shim image for cross-distro compatibility.
elaine (sec-eng): Decision: Patch and rebuild base images + rebuild impacted sidecars with musl flags where feasible. For non-trivial apps, add fallback to glibc-compat shim.
anil (eng-platform): Updating pipeline: add `image-compat-check` step and `annotation: rebuild_reason=CVE-2026-0XXX`. Will also record `signer_key_version` in metadata.
jia (eng-infra): Promoting canary to staging now. Audit log entry: `{"job":"rebuild/base-ssl-compat-1945","phase":"canary","image":"sha256:abc123...","kms_key_version":"1"}` (sent to secure-bucket).
eleaine typo (ignored): (none)
everyone: small follow-ups: please add test gaps to the runbook.
elaine (sec-eng): I'll open a short postmortem runbook PR with steps, RBAC checklist, and a template for audit queries. Expect PR in 2 hours.
sasha (product-security): Thanks all — coordinating disclosure once we confirm canary stability.
ryan (eng-runtime): Monitoring checklist pushed to ops dashboard.
jia (eng-infra): KMS rotation deferred by 8 hours to avoid signer key disruptions.
elaine (sec-eng): Closing loop: timeline — patch applied, canary running, manual sidecar rebuilds in progress, promotion target 2026-04-01 10:00 UTC if green. If anything blocks, ping this thread.
